gallery.filename: A far view of the Itsukushima shrine off Hiroshima (49495487196).jpg
gallery.title: File:A far view of the Itsukushima shrine off Hiroshima (49495487196).jpg
gallery.artist: shankar s. from Poona (pune), India, India
gallery.description: We are almost there now, and this is a far view of the Itsukushima shrine off the Hiroshima coast in Japan. Extending from the sides of the haraiden (main hall in Shinto Buddhist temples) of the main shrine is a noh (traditional Japanese masked drama with dance and song, evolved from Shinto rites) stage which dates from 1590. Noh theatre performances have long been used to pay homage to the gods through the ritual acting out of key events in Shinto myth. On September 5, 2004, the shrine was severely damaged by Typhoon Songda. The boardwalks and roof were partially destroyed, and the shrine was temporarily closed for repairs. Today anyone can go visit the shrine for only 300 yen. Itsukushima jinja was the chief Shinto shrine (ichinomiya) of Aki Province during the heydays of the Itsukushima shrine. (Hiroshima,Japan, Apr/ May 2019)

gallery.filename: Counters at the Itsukushima shrine to buy lucky charms and other religious doo dads (49495480271).jpg
gallery.title: File:Counters at the Itsukushima shrine to buy lucky charms and other religious doo dads (49495480271).jpg
gallery.artist: shankar s. from Poona (pune), India, India
gallery.description: I am done with the Itsukushima shrine and it is time to leave now. I am really short of time as I have an over hour long trip to Hiroshima station to catch my Shinkansen train back to Hiroshima. On my way out, I spotted this standard feature in all the Japanese temples I have seen so far- a series of counters to buy religious doo dads, temple related souvenirs and good luck charms. I observed that these counters were always heavily subscribed as seems to be the case here too. The items on sale are not exactly cheap bit I guess the proceeds go to the maintenance and upkeep of the temple. The items on sale are displayed in the frames you see here, suspended above the counters. (Hiroshima,Japan, Apr/ May 2019)

gallery.filename: Another of the sanctums in the Itsukushima shrine (49495702587).jpg
gallery.title: File:Another of the sanctums in the Itsukushima shrine (49495702587).jpg
gallery.artist: shankar s. from Poona (pune), India, India
gallery.description: I am leaving the Itsukushima shrine just off the Hiroshima coast in Japan, and as I leave, I pass another one of the three sanctums in the temple. The Itsukushima shrine is dedicated to the three daughters of Susano-o no Mikoto- they are  Ichikishimahime no mikoto, Tagorihime no mikoto, and Tagitsuhime no mikoto. Otherwise known as the sanjoshin or three female deities, these Shinto deities are the goddesses of seas and storms. Kiyomori believed the goddesses to be the manifestations of Kannon and hence the island was understood as the home of the bodhisattva Kannon. More notes about the Itsukushima shrine appeared earlier in this album. (see previous pictures).  (Hiroshima,Japan, Apr/ May 2019)
